title: Affine pushout ring and first tensor sections with both actions
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Put $A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, $\rho:\mathcal O_X\to A$, and let $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$, $t_0=f^{-1}\rho$, and $e:f^{-1}A\to\mathcal O_U$ be the structure map, inverse-image map and counit. Let $B$ be a commutative ring sheaf, with $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$, $t:f^{-1}A\to B$, $\epsilon:B\to\mathcal O_U$, such that $(r_0,t_0,b,t)$ is a pushout and $b\epsilon=1$, $t\epsilon=e$. Sheaves of modules and tensor pullback are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with the canonical adjunction of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Write $S=\operatorname{res}_{\rho}$ and $I=f^{-1}$. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ agree on objects and maps with change of rings along $t$ after $I$. Let $\kappa:P\operatorname{res}_b\simeq Sf^*$ satisfy, after this object identification, $\kappa_G^{-1}(\operatorname{unit}_{SG}(n))=\operatorname{sheafify}(1\otimes\eta_G(n))$ on each inverse-image open, where $\eta_G$ is the additive inverse-image unit. For a quasi-coherent $A$-module $G$ [pqf-def-coherent] and affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $W=f^{-1}V$, $D=\mathcal O_X(V)$, $C=\mathcal O_U(W)$, $N=G(V)$, $E=B(W)$ and $M=P(G)(W)$. The $D$-actions on $N$ and $M$ are restricted along $f^\sharp_V$ and $b_W f^\sharp_V$ respectively. There exist a ring homomorphism $\delta:C\to E$ and a $D$-linear equivalence $p:C\otimes_D N\simeq M$ such that $\epsilon_W\delta=1_C$, every $r\in E$ is a finite sum $\sum_i b_W(c_i)\delta(d_i)$ with $c_i,d_i\in C$, and for all $c,d\in C$, $n\in N$ one has $b_W(c)p(d\otimes n)=p(cd\otimes n)$, $\delta(c)p(d\otimes n)=p(d\otimes cn)$, and $p(1\otimes n)=\kappa_G^{-1}(\operatorname{unit}_{SG,V}(n))$. No final extension module or gamma occurs in this assertion.

proof.text: Pushforward of the unit module along affine f makes A quasi-coherent over O_X. Restriction of scalars makes G quasi-coherent over O_X. On the affine preimage W, apply the canonical affine pullback-section comparison to SG, commute its tensor factors, and follow by kappa inverse. This gives the D-linear equivalence p; its C-linearity is the b-action formula and its unit formula is the canonical pullback unit.

Apply the same affine comparison to the algebra A. The pushout universal property identifies B with the sheafification of O_U tensor over f inverse O_X with f inverse A. The canonical section map is multiplicative and sends the two inclusions to b and t after the inverse-image unit, so on W it gives B(W) = C tensor_D C. Let delta be the second inclusion. The equation t followed by epsilon = e and the inverse-image triangle identity give epsilon(delta(c)) = c. Tensor induction gives a finite additive sum of b(c)delta(d) for every section of B(W), including negative terms by putting the minus sign in the first factor.

On the unsheafified section tensor product the two actions are b(c)(d tensor n)=cd tensor n and delta(c)(d tensor n)=d tensor cn. The inverse-image unit is compatible with the A-action. The hP normalization identifies kappa inverse of the canonical pullback unit with sheafification of 1 tensor eta(n), and C-linearity extends that equality to all pure tensors. The actions therefore transfer through p with exactly the displayed formulas. All identities are additive and balanced, so they extend through sheafification and to the empty open and zero rings.
